title: New Orleans Bourbon Street truck attack
description: On January 1, 2025, Shamsud-Din Jabbar drove a pickup truck into crowds celebrating New Year on Bourbon Street, then opened fire, killing 14 people and injuring dozens before being fatally shot by police. The FBI classified the attack as a terrorist act inspired by the Islamic State, to which Jabbar pledged allegiance in videos posted before the attack.

title: Los Angeles wildfires (Palisades and Eaton fires)
description: The Palisades and Eaton fires began in Los Angeles County on January 7, 2025 local time and were contained on January 31. CAL FIRE records 31 civilian deaths and 16,264 destroyed structures across the two fires.

title: Gul Plaza shopping mall fire
description: A fire broke out at the Gul Plaza shopping centre in Karachi on the night of 17 January 2026. Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority subsequently reported at least 80 deaths and dozens of injuries; an earlier inquiry report counted 79 deaths. The fire spread through the multistorey commercial building.

title: Nigeria fuel tanker explosion in Suleja
description: A fuel tanker accident and explosion at Dikko junction in Niger State on January 18, 2025 killed people gathered around spilled fuel. NEMA reported 98 deaths and 69 injuries in its January 28 update.

title: Gaza war ceasefire
description: A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect on January 19, 2025, after 15 months of war in which the Gaza Health Ministry reported more than 47,000 Palestinians killed and most of the territory's population displaced. The first phase of the agreement included releases of hostages and prisoners before hostilities later resumed.

review.note: OCHA establishes that the ceasefire took effect January 19 at 11:15 local time, not its January 22 publication date, and reports hostage/prisoner releases. The 47,000 is a cumulative war toll, not deaths caused by a ceasefire; an exact matching January 19 cutoff is not established here. This overlaps the existing 2023 and 2024 Gaza death records. A later cumulative report cannot verify the number on the ceasefire date. Do not publish a deaths-bearing ceasefire row until its toll scope and duplicate treatment are resolved.

title: Antioch High School shooting
description: On January 22, 2025, 17-year-old Solomon Henderson shot and killed one student and wounded another in the Antioch High School cafeteria in Nashville, then died by suicide. Police reported ten shots within 17 seconds.

title: West Bandung landslide
location: West Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia
description: Heavy rain triggered a landslide in Pasirlangu village, West Bandung Regency, at about 02:30 local time on 24 January 2026 (23 January UTC), burying homes. By 10 February, West Java police had identified 80 victims. Identification of additional remains was continuing.

title: M23 capture of Goma
location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Between January 23 and 30, 2025, Rwandan-backed M23 rebels captured Goma, the capital of North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, after heavy fighting against the national army, UN and SADC peacekeepers, and allied militias; the UN estimated about 2,900 people were killed and another 2,900 wounded, with hundreds of thousands displaced.

review.note: The February 5 UN briefing, reproduced by ANSA, supports a provisional 2,900 dead: 2,000 bodies collected from streets and 900 in morgues. This is not a final January 23-30-only total. UNICEF describes January 26-28 fighting and control of most of Goma by January 28; the January 27 UN briefing describes an ongoing battle, while the later experts' annex calls January 27 full conquest. The same report also cites narrower health-facility fatality/injury counts. The exact capture-date framing and matching casualty period remain unsettled; do not silently resolve them with publication dates.

title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse
location: Rubaya, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Heavy rain caused a landslide and mine collapses at the Rubaya coltan mining complex in North Kivu on 28 January 2026. Rebel-appointed authorities reported at least 200 deaths. A civil-society representative subsequently estimated roughly 400 deaths; that higher figure remained provisional and was not limited to miners.

review.note: The roughly 400 figure is a provisional civil-society estimate, not a confirmed count of miners alone; AP reported at least 200. March 3 is supported by Reuters (published March 4), but that separate collapse has a disputed toll and should not be folded into January's deaths. Exact January onset time unavailable. The numeric field still reflects a provisional estimate; a confirmed comparable toll and January UTC onset remain unresolved.

title: Unity oilfield plane crash
description: On January 29, 2025, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by Eagle Air on behalf of Light Air Services crashed shortly after takeoff from the Unity oilfield airstrip in Unity State, South Sudan, while carrying oil workers to Juba; 20 of the 21 people on board were killed.

title: Balochistan Liberation Army attacks
description: Between 29 January and 5 February 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Army launched a coordinated series of attacks across Balochistan province, Pakistan, including raids on a police station and banks in Kharan, a security post in Panjgur and military positions in Harnai. The week-long campaign left at least 225 people dead, including 36 civilians and 2 security personnel, while Pakistani forces reported killing 216 militants in retaliatory raids.

review.note: January 29 is the military operation's beginning, not the coordinated BLA assault (January 31). The reported components are 216 militants, 36 civilians and 22 security personnel = 274, not 225; all are military-reported, not independently confirmed. The original identity key is retained for audit only. The proposed scope is a multi-day campaign, not a proven single-day BLA attack. Its start date must not be presented as the date of all 274 deaths; assault versus military-operation allocation remains unresolved.

title: Potomac River mid-air collision (American Airlines Flight 5342)
description: At about 01:48 UTC on January 30, 2025 (the evening of January 29 locally), PSA Airlines Flight 5342 and a US Army UH-60L helicopter collided near Reagan Washington National Airport and fell into the Potomac River. All 64 people on the airliner and three helicopter crew members died.

title: Kwara State attacks
description: Armed extremists attacked Woro and Nuku in Kaiama, Kwara State, on the evening of 3 February 2026. Local officials and the Red Cross reported at least 162 deaths, while the state government initially gave a lower count. Homes were burned and residents abducted. Reports differed over the attackers' affiliation, and no group immediately claimed responsibility.

title: Islamabad mosque suicide bombing
description: An attacker opened fire at the gates of the Khadija Tul Kubra Shia mosque in Islamabad's Tarlai area during Friday prayers on 6 February 2026 before detonating explosives. The death toll subsequently rose to 36. More than 100 people were injured. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

title: Tumbler Ridge school shooting
description: An 18-year-old former student killed eight people in Tumbler Ridge on 10 February 2026: her mother and 11-year-old brother at a home, and five students and a teacher at the secondary school. The perpetrator also died by suicide, bringing the total dead to nine. Twenty-seven people were reported injured.

title: Abiemnom massacre
description: Armed attackers raided Abiemnom in South Sudan's Ruweng Administrative Area on 1 March 2026. Local authorities reported 169 deaths, including 90 civilians. The UN mission said about 1,000 people sought shelter at its base. Accounts differed over the attackers' affiliation and the number injured.
sources: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

title: Bahia Blanca flash floods
description: Flash flooding struck Bahia Blanca and surrounding areas on March 7, 2025, after 290 mm of rain in 12 hours. The confirmed death toll reached 18 after identification of the last missing child in May.

title: Syrian coastal massacres of Alawites
description: A Reuters investigation documented 1,479 Alawites killed at 40 sites during the March 7-9, 2025 massacres in Syria's coastal region. Its reporting linked attackers through a chain of command to figures serving alongside the country's new leadership; the count does not include all deaths in the wider fighting.

title: Gamo Zone floods and landslides
description: On 10 March 2026, days of heavy rainfall in the Gamo Zone of South Ethiopia triggered widespread flash floods and landslides that killed at least 125 people. The disaster struck farming communities in the southern highlands, destroying homes, roads and farmland across multiple villages.

review.note: 125 deaths supported; sources date the sequence March 9-10, March 10, or early March 11. Exact UTC onset and road/farmland damage remain unresolved.

title: Jaffar Express hijacking
description: Baloch Liberation Army militants hijacked the Jaffar Express in Balochistan on March 11, 2025. Pakistan's military reported 31 victims killed, 354 hostages rescued and 33 attackers killed when the operation ended the following day.

title: Kocani nightclub fire
description: A fire at the Pulse nightclub in Kocani on March 16, 2025 killed 63 people and injured more than 200, according to figures cited in court indictments. Investigators reported that pyrotechnics ignited flammable ceiling foam in a venue lacking adequate fire safety provisions.

title: South Korea wildfire outbreak
description: Wildfires began in southeastern South Korea on March 21, 2025 and spread across several areas, including Uiseong and Sancheong. World Weather Attribution's April 30 account reported 32 deaths in the March outbreak; Copernicus also reports 32 deaths and around 5,000 buildings destroyed.

title: Myanmar earthquake (magnitude 7.7)
description: On March 28, 2025, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Sagaing and Mandalay in Myanmar along the Sagaing Fault, collapsing buildings and infrastructure and also killing 18 people in Bangkok, Thailand. Myanmar's military government reported about 3,770 dead, while independent Myanmar media estimates exceeded 5,000, and the true toll was widely considered higher.

review.note: The March 28 M7.7 earthquake is well supported, but 3,770 is not a final reconciled death count. Myanmar's government reported 3,782 as of August 20, 2025 for six affected regions/states; UNICEF's May 2 report used 3,835 from another reporting stream. Independent Myanmar-media estimates were substantially higher, and the Thai 18-death figure is an early snapshot (ADRC already reports 83 Thailand deaths in its May 7 snapshot). National, cross-border and independent counts need a consistent cutoff and scope. Do not equate the government count with the true whole-event toll or retain 18 as a final Thai total.

title: Jilli market airstrike
description: A Nigerian airstrike hit Jilli market near the Borno-Yobe border on 11 April 2026. Amnesty International reported at least 100 civilians killed, citing survivors and medical contacts. Other estimates were higher. The military said it had targeted militants; accounts of the strike and the casualty total remained disputed.

review.note: April 11 event, April 12 publication. 100 is a rights-group toll, not official final count. Military defended the operation; exact UTC onset unavailable. A single verified UTC onset and reconciliation of the competing casualty accounts remain unavailable; the attributed minimum is not a confirmed final total.

title: Afghanistan flash floods
description: In late April 2025, heavy rains triggered flash floods across northern Afghanistan, with the worst destruction in Baghlan Province, where entire villages were swept away; at least 150 people were killed across the affected provinces per BBC reporting, while the World Food Programme estimated more than 300 dead and hundreds more injured.

review.note: Searches did not establish an April 27, 2025 Baghlan flood with these fatalities. The 150 official/300-plus WFP reporting pattern instead matches the May 10, 2024 northern Afghanistan floods, confirmed by contemporaneous May 2024 UN and news reports. The assigned data already has a May 2024 Baghlan event. This suggests a misdated duplicate, not proof that no flooding occurred in 2025. Do not automatically move this row to May 2024 or count both; identity, date and casualty scope require reconciliation.

title: Qinyuan coal mine explosion
description: On 22 May 2026, an explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Qinyuan County, Shanxi Province, China, killed at least 82 miners, the worst coal-mining blast in China in more than a decade. The blast in one of China's major coal-producing regions prompted a state investigation into safety practices.

title: Mindanao earthquake
description: On 8 June 2026, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck offshore Sarangani province, Mindanao, on the Cotabato Trench, killing at least 106 people (107 per final tallies) and injuring 1,320, with 7 missing. More than 121,000 homes were damaged or destroyed and damage exceeded ₱71 billion (US$1.44 billion). General Santos, Sarangani, South Cotabato and Davao Occidental were hardest hit, and coastal uplift of up to 2 metres damaged marine habitats across Sarangani Bay.

review.note: 07:37 local June 8 = 23:37 UTC June 7. Date-only correction; final 107 deaths, injuries/missing, housing totals, PHP 71bn loss and uplift claims remain unverified.

title: Air India Flight 171 crash
description: Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 bound for London Gatwick, crashed shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad at about 08:09 UTC on June 12, 2025, striking B. J. Medical College hostel buildings. The official preliminary report records 241 deaths among 242 people aboard and 19 deaths on the ground.
sources: Ministry of Civil Aviation parliamentary answer

title: Israel-Iran war (Twelve-Day War)
description: On June 13, 2025, Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Iranian military and nuclear facilities and killing commanders and nuclear scientists; Iran responded with more than 550 ballistic missiles and over 1,000 drones fired at Israel over 12 days. Roughly 33 people were killed in Israel and about 1,060 in Iran, according to the respective authorities.

review.note: June 13-24 is supported, but 1,093 is not a reconciled total. The original roughly 1,060 in Iran is a July 7 official update; the spokesperson raised it to at least 1,062 on July 22. HRANA reported 1,190 using a separate casualty register. Reuters reports 28 killed in Israel, not the original 33; inclusion of indirect or later deaths is not established for the latter. Do not average competing counts or treat different reporting dates as final same-scope totals. The 550-plus missile claim is supported by AP, but the drone count was not established here. Withhold until the overall numeric toll and scope are resolved.

title: Shooting of Minnesota state legislators
location: Brooklyn Park and Champlin, Minnesota, United States
description: On June 14, 2025, Vance Boelter killed Minnesota Representative Melissa Hortman and her husband Mark at their Brooklyn Park home and wounded Senator John Hoffman and his wife Yvette in Champlin. After his arrest, he pleaded guilty to federal murder and related charges on June 11, 2026; the separate state prosecution remained pending as of September 21, 2026.

title: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
description: Two earthquakes, reported at magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela on 24 June 2026, causing widespread destruction, particularly in La Guaira. Official figures cited by UNICEF recorded 6,125 deaths as of 3 August. Homes and infrastructure were damaged and many residents displaced.

title: Angara Airlines Flight 2311 crash
description: On July 24, 2025, an Angara Airlines Antonov An-24 operating Flight 2311 crashed near Tynda in Russia's Amur region while approaching its destination. All 42 passengers and six crew members died.

title: Gansu flash flood at Weiyuan scenic area
description: A flash flood struck a scenic area in Weiyuan County, Dingxi City, on the afternoon of 26 July 2026, killing 25 people and injuring 23. China's national disaster commission said it would oversee an investigation into the disaster and urged Gansu Province to strengthen disaster prevention, mitigation and relief capacity.

title: Kumamoto earthquake
description: An earthquake measured at magnitude 7.1 by Japan's Meteorological Agency struck Kumamoto at 16:27 local time on 28 July 2026. Prefectural figures as of 3 August recorded 38 deaths, 98 injuries and 8,383 evacuees. Damage included an explosion and collapse at Aeon Mall in Kashima and a chimney collapse at a paper mill in Yatsushiro.

title: Firefighting helicopter crash in San Juan kills seven
description: A Bell 412 helicopter contracted by Argentina's Federal Emergency Agency crashed near Ischigualasto Provincial Park in San Juan on 29 July 2026, killing all seven occupants. It had previously taken part in training and was travelling toward La Rioja to assist firefighting operations. Contact was lost at about 10:26 local time.

title: Militant drone-and-ambush attack on police checkpoint in Hangu
description: Militants, blamed by police on the Pakistani Taliban (TTP), launched a drone strike and ambush on the Khazina Banda police checkpoint in Hangu district on the evening of July 29, 2026, in an assault that also involved an attack on a neighbouring checkpost. Eleven police officers, including a deputy superintendent of police, were killed as the death toll rose through the following morning, with initial reports citing 9 to 10 officers dead and at least 28 injured; authorities said 15 attackers were also killed in the ensuing gunfight. It was the second major assault on security forces in the area within a week amid escalating attacks in the Afghanistan–Pakistan border region.

review.note: July 29 and 11 police dead supported; attackers killed differ (AP 15, ARY eight). Drone detail, prior assault comparison and precise UTC onset not established.

title: US–Saudi airstrikes kill 20 Iran-backed militiamen in Iraq as US strikes on Iran resume
description: As part of the 2026 Iran war, US Central Command and Saudi forces carried out joint strikes on positions of Iran-backed militias in Iraq on July 29, 2026, killing 20 Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) militants, including several Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) members, according to the PMF. The same day, after a six-day pause, the US military resumed heavy waves of strikes against dozens of IRGC targets inside Iran in retaliation for an attempted missile attack on US forces in the Middle East a day earlier, an escalation that prompted Iranian retaliatory strikes on Kuwait days later.
sources: Wikipedia: July 2026 United States strikes against Iran

review.note: PMF reported 20 members killed. IRGC advisers may be additional. Overnight July 28-29 requires UTC check; resumed Iran strikes and causal link to Kuwait not fully established.

title: Wildfires in southern Greece kill three firefighters
location: Rethymno, Crete and Gytheio, Laconia, Greece
description: Three firefighters died during wildfire response operations in southern Greece on 29 July 2026. Two died in a fire in the Rethymno region of Crete. A third was found unconscious near a fire in the Gytheio area and pronounced dead in hospital; authorities had not established the cause of his death.

title: Broad Peak avalanche kills ten climbers
description: An avalanche struck ten climbers on Broad Peak in Pakistan's Karakoram range on the morning of 30 July 2026. All ten, including Nirmal Purja, were subsequently confirmed dead. Recovery operations continued after the first bodies were located, with weather and terrain hindering access.

title: Coal mine explosion in Balochistan
description: A methane gas explosion ripped through a coal mine in Balochistan province on 30 July, killing at least 34 miners. Rescue officials recovered 32 bodies and said two workers remained trapped in an inaccessible section of the mine.

review.note: AP reports 34 dead, 32 recovered and two to retrieve. July 30 occurrence versus July 31 publication distinguished. Exact time unavailable but no evidence of UTC crossover. Absence of evidence of a crossover does not establish the UTC date; withhold pending an onset time or sufficiently specific time-of-day account.

title: Russia launches massive missile and drone strike on Ukraine
location: Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine
description: In the early hours of July 30, 2026, Russia launched one of its largest combined strikes of the war, firing dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles and hundreds of drones (President Zelensky cited over 70 missiles and 280 drones) at cities across Ukraine, with damage reported from east to west in Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih. At least 10 civilians, including children, were killed and more than 50 injured, including six people killed by a ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih and a family of six killed in a village hit by a suspected North Korean missile; NATO scrambled jets in response and a stray Russian cruise missile briefly entered Polish airspace.

review.note: 70 missiles/280 drones supported; Reuters nine deaths, EFE earlier eight, versus record ten. Family and Kryvyi Rih totals may overlap. Polish incursion and UTC onset not confirmed.

title: Flash floods and landslides in Dien Bien Province
description: Flash floods and landslides struck Dien Bien Province early on 1 August 2025 local time (31 July UTC), after heavy rain. A subsequent provincial tally reported ten deaths and seven injuries. Homes and roads were damaged and several communities isolated.

title: Apartment building fire kills four in Changsha
description: A fire broke out at 03:54 local time on 1 August at a high-rise residential building in the Poly Lugu Linyu compound, Yuelu District, Changsha, killing four people and injuring two. Firefighters rescued six people from the building, but four later died of their injuries in hospital.

review.note: Fire service statement reproduced by Xinhua gives 03:54 August 1 local = 19:54 July 31 UTC; six rescued, four died by August 2, two receiving treatment. All material claims match. Only one retrieved publication/source chain; a second independent link is still needed before canonical source replacement. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

title: Calabar flood and landslide crisis
description: Weeks of torrential rain in July 2026 caused flooding and landslides across Calabar, killing at least 10 people, including a baby swept away by floodwater and a father buried in mud. The rains destroyed homes, triggered landslides that killed families, and cut off access roads; the toll was cumulative through the end of July.

review.note: Ten is a month-long total published August 1, not deaths on July 31. Primary report supports flooding/landslides but no dated ten-person tally. A defensible onset anchor and overlap with individual incidents remain unresolved.

title: Iranian strike on Chinese company building in Kuwait kills worker
description: Kuwait's Defence Ministry said an Iranian attack hit a building belonging to a Chinese company in northern Kuwait on 30 July 2026, killing one worker and causing substantial damage.

review.note: Fatality belongs to July 30 company-building strike, not July 31 base claim; exact clock time unavailable. The proposed July 30 is the reported local occurrence date; UTC conversion remains unverified.

title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv
description: Russian forces launched a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv shortly after midnight on 1 August local time, killing at least nine people and injuring more than 20, including children. Fires broke out across four districts and rescue operations continued through the night.

review.note: Nine dead and 33 injured supported for overnight July 31-August 1. Exact onset for UTC conversion not established. Appears duplicate of 'Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills ten' dated August 1; reconcile and retain only one incident.

title: Terrorist attack on labourers in Kulgam
description: Gunmen shot two workers from Chhattisgarh at a brick kiln in Kelam, Kulgam district, on the evening of 31 July 2026. One died initially and the second later died in hospital, bringing the death toll to two.

title: Assam flood death toll reaches 82
description: Assam's disaster authority reported a cumulative monsoon-flood death toll of 82 by late 31 July 2026. Reports published the next morning said roughly 193,000 people in five districts remained affected. This is a season-to-date toll, not deaths on one day.

review.note: 82 was announced late Friday July 31, reported Saturday August 1. It is season-to-date, not daily deaths. Current affected population was about 193000; 1.1m may refer to another snapshot. District death breakdown not corroborated. The proposed July 31 is a reporting snapshot, not a verified onset. Its Assam component overlaps the India-wide monsoon tally; publication requires a defensible non-overlapping episode boundary.

title: Bombing at Moscow restaurant kills five
description: A bomb exploded near the Balzi Rossi restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in Moscow on the evening of 1 August 2026. Authorities initially reported three deaths, including the woman carrying the device, a security guard and a visitor. A subsequent Russian embassy statement reported five dead and 19 injured.

title: Israeli strikes kill at least seven in Gaza
description: Gaza's civil defence reported seven people killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip since dawn on 1 August 2026. An Israeli strike also destroyed medical supplies stored for Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, according to hospital and Palestinian health officials.

title: Plane crash near Nazca kills 13
description: A small plane crashed in farmland about 6 km from the city of Nazca in Peru's southern Ica region on Saturday, killing all 13 on board — 11 tourists plus the pilot and co-pilot. Local media reported that seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards were among the dead; the flight was on a tour route over the Nazca Lines.

review.note: August 1 crash, 13 occupants and tourist nationalities corroborated. Exact six-kilometre location and aircraft timing/UTC not independently established; avoid full verification.

title: Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills ten
description: In a heavy ballistic missile attack early on Saturday, Russia struck Kyiv and the surrounding region, killing 10 people and wounding more than 30. It was the second major attack on the capital that week; President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had run out of Patriot interceptor missiles.

review.note: Likely duplicate of July 31 'Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv'. Sources report nine, not ten, in the overnight July 31-August 1 attack; ten may be borrowed from July 30 nationwide strikes. Merge after establishing onset; do not sum both records.

title: Shooting at In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls
description: A shooting near an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls on the afternoon of 1 August 2026 left three people dead and seven injured, according to the city's public update. Police said the immediate threat had ended and the investigation was continuing.

review.note: City and local public radio update injuries to seven. 14:30 MDT is 20:30 UTC August 1. Retrieved accounts vary over whether three deaths include gunman; retain reported three without claiming three homicide victims. Resolve victim/perpetrator breakdown separately. Publication is withheld until the victim/perpetrator scope of the total is reconciled.

title: Taliban police report killing seven alleged robbers in Kabul
description: Taliban police said seven men accused of armed robbery were killed during an operation in Kabul's Police District 8 on 1 August 2026. Police described a confrontation at about 21:00 local time. A former Afghan justice minister subsequently described the killings as extrajudicial; the police account was not independently established.

title: Drone strike on Darfur community court kills at least 46, rights group reports
description: A drone strike hit Zawiya Ghara community court in North Darfur during a court session on 2 August 2026. Emergency Lawyers initially reported at least 35 deaths. Darfur Victims Support Organization later reported 46 civilian deaths and seven injuries in preliminary documentation based on interviews with families and witnesses. Rights groups attributed the strike to the Sudanese army.

title: Firefighting helicopters collide in Greece killing two
description: Two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air on Sunday while battling a wind-driven wildfire west of Athens, and one caught fire and crashed. A Greek and a Danish crew member died; the two survivors — a Greek and a British national — were taken to hospital in Athens.

title: Israeli strikes kill 18 in Gaza
description: Israeli airstrikes across Gaza on 2 August 2026 killed at least 18 Palestinians, including children, according to medics. Strikes hit Gaza City, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis. The toll may overlap the 18 newly killed people in the health ministry's next-day 24-hour bulletin and must not be counted again.

title: Russian glide bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia
description: Russian aircraft dropped eight glide bombs on residential districts of Zaporizhzhia within 90 minutes on Sunday evening, killing a 71-year-old woman, wounding 31 people — including a 16-year-old girl — and damaging 22 apartment buildings in four districts of the city.

title: Suicide bombing at anti-militant rally kills 14 in Swat
description: A suicide bomber targeted protesters gathered outside a police station in Kabal, Swat, on Sunday, killing at least 14 people — including eight police officers — and wounding more than two dozen others, officials said. The rally was part of an anti-militant peace campaign in northwestern Pakistan.

review.note: August 2 Kabal rally attack supported. Totals differ: 14, 15 and later secondary 17; police/civilian breakdown and injured counts vary. Do not combine incompatible snapshots. Exact onset unavailable.

title: Ukraine strikes deep inside Russia kill eight
description: Large-scale Ukrainian drone strikes on targets deep inside Russia on Sunday killed at least eight people, including at logistics warehouses of retailer Wildberries in the Moscow region. Russia said it shot down 635 UAVs overnight, and the acting governor of the border Belgorod region reported four dead in strikes on civilian areas.

review.note: DW supports eight nationwide but lists Udmurtia and Belgorod, and depicts Wildberries in Samara, not Moscow. AP's next-day account reports nine. Location composition, 635 interceptions, Belgorod four and UTC coverage require reconciliation.

title: Drone crash on Gelendzhik-area beach kills eight
description: A drone crashed onto a beach at Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik on the morning of 3 August 2026. Later reporting put the toll at eight deaths, including four children, with 58 injured. Russia attributed the drone to Ukraine; whether air defences caused it to crash remained uncertain.

title: Israeli fire kills 19 Palestinians in Gaza
description: At least 19 Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire over 24 hours, including 18 killed by Israeli forces and one who died of wounds from an earlier attack, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. The deaths brought the number of Palestinians killed since the ceasefire to more than 1,250.

review.note: Ministry's August 3 release supports 18 newly killed plus one previous-wound death, not 19 deaths necessarily occurring August 3. Likely overlaps August 2 entry's 18. Cannot count both totals independently; exact rolling-window cutoff and unique victims unresolved.

title: Israeli strike kills two in Gaza City
description: An Israeli airstrike targeted a vehicle southwest of Gaza City on Monday evening, killing two Palestinians in the Sheikh Ajlin area, in another violation of the ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, medical sources said.

title: Landslide kills 14 at Ethiopian monastery
description: Heavy rainfall triggered a landslide that buried worshippers gathered at Tsadqane Debre Mitmaq St. Mary Monastery in Amhara's North Shewa Zone, killing 14 people and injuring at least seven, with an unknown number still missing as search and rescue efforts continued.

review.note: AP's full report supports date, monastery, region, rain, 14 deaths, seven injuries and people unaccounted for. 07:00 local = 04:00 UTC August 3. One retrieved source chain; obtain second independent URL before replacing canonical sources. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

title: Russian guided bombs kill three in Sumy
description: Russian guided aerial bombs struck Sumy between 02:08 and 02:17 local time on 4 August 2026 (3 August UTC). The attack killed two girls aged five and ten and a 75-year-old woman, according to Ukrainian reports, and injured other residents. Homes and civilian infrastructure were damaged.

title: CRPF officer shooting in Assam kills four
description: A CRPF officer shot two colleagues dead and seriously wounded another at the 34th Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, before killing himself; the wounded personnel member later died in hospital, bringing the death toll to four, police said.

review.note: Two colleagues and perpetrator dead, one injured supported; August 12 follow-up still describes three. No support located for injured colleague's later death. Morning August 4 may require exact clock for UTC boundary. Any rewrite must use 'died by suicide' without method.

title: Israeli fire kills two in Gaza
description: Two more Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire in Gaza over 24 hours, with ten others injured, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, bringing the death toll since October 7, 2023 to 73,377. Some victims remained trapped under rubble beyond the reach of rescue crews.

review.note: August 4 is bulletin date; two newly reported deaths may include the August 3 vehicle strike. Cumulative 73377 corroborated, but exact death dates/unique victims and full injury/rubble claims not established.

title: Lightning strike kills footballer in Thailand
description: A lightning strike during a Golok FA Cup match at Santiphap Stadium in Sungai Golok, Narathiwat, on the afternoon of 4 August 2026 killed 24-year-old Yala FC player Sofwan Awae. At least nine others were reported injured.

title: Russian drone strike on Mykolaiv kills elderly woman
description: Russian drones attacked the southern port city of Mykolaiv overnight, killing an 89-year-old woman and injuring seven people, including two children. Two private houses were destroyed and several other buildings were damaged.

review.note: Victim age, seven injured including two children, and two destroyed homes supported. Night of August 3-4 not precise enough for UTC day; do not use publication date as onset.

title: Serviceman kills four in shooting near Sevastopol
description: A Russian serviceman opened fire on fellow soldiers and civilians in the village of Khmelnitskoye near Sevastopol, killing four people - one soldier and three civilians aged 59, 64 and 71 - and wounding four others before being detained, Sevastopol Governor Mikhail Razvozhayev said.

review.note: Four dead (one soldier/three civilians), four injured and detention supported. AP explicitly says governor did not specify when it happened: August 4 is report date, not proven occurrence date. Victim ages not established.

title: Ukrainian drone strike on Moscow region kills five
description: A Ukrainian drone strike on an industrial zone in Novoselki near Chekhov, outside Moscow, started fires at an industrial site and killed five people, wounding at least six others, Moscow Region Governor Andrei Vorobyov said. The attack was part of an escalation of long-range drone strikes exchanged between Russia and Ukraine.

review.note: Governor's five dead/six injured and Novoselki/Chekhov supported. Overnight onset not precise enough to establish August 3 versus 4 UTC; sources share governor statement rather than independent casualty confirmation.

title: Explosion in southern Lebanon kills two Israeli soldiers
description: Two Israeli reservists from Battalion 2855 of the 55th Reserve Paratroopers Brigade were killed and four seriously wounded in an explosion during an operation in Majdal Zoun on 5 August 2026, the Israeli military announced the following day. The circumstances of the explosive device were under investigation.

title: India monsoon floods and landslides kill more than 100 since July
description: An official tally released on August 5 showed that floods and landslides triggered by monsoon rains had killed at least 133 people across India since the beginning of July: 87 in Assam (47 in Sivasagar district alone), 31 in Jammu and Kashmir, and 15 in Kerala, with seven people still missing and more than 10,000 in relief camps.

review.note: AFP supports 133 since early July, including 87 in Assam. August 5 is release date, not event date. Assam portion overlaps the 82-death Assam record. Must choose non-overlapping disaster scopes and establish onset; do not add both full tolls.

title: Israeli airstrike on south Lebanon kills one
description: An Israeli drone strike hit the roof of a prayer hall at a cemetery in Tebnine, Bint Jbeil district, on 5 August 2026. Lebanon's Health Ministry reported one person killed and twelve injured, updating an initial report of eleven injuries. The strike came as a round of Lebanese-Israeli talks in Rome concluded.

title: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza
description: Israel killed four more Palestinians in Gaza over 24 hours, bringing the war's death toll to 73,381, the Gaza Health Ministry said. Since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025, Israeli violations have killed 1,254 Palestinians and injured 4,121.

review.note: All quoted ministry totals supported as an August 5 reporting snapshot, but rolling 24h fatalities cannot all be dated August 5. Unique victims and overlap with incident-level entries not established.

title: Mass shooting in Caswell County, North Carolina kills three
location: Caswell County, North Carolina, United States
description: A mass shooting at a rural home in Caswell County, North Carolina, left three family members dead - including the suspected shooter - and a fourth relative hospitalized, according to the Caswell County Sheriff's Office and the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation.

title: Mudslide buries household in Zhashui County, Shaanxi
description: A sudden mudslide triggered by days of heavy rainfall buried members of a household in Xingping township, Zhashui County, while they were clearing water near their home on August 5. One person was confirmed dead and two remained missing; continuous rain from July 30 to August 5 reached 321.4 mm in the county.

review.note: Xinhua's August 6 dispatch quotes the county flood-control headquarters: the household was buried August 5, with one confirmed dead and two missing. It also supports the July 30-August 5 maximum rainfall figure. Missing people are not included in lives_lost. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

title: Rain-triggered house collapse kills six in Pratapgarh, India
description: A house collapsed during heavy rain in Mahuli, Pratapgarh district, at about 2 a.m. local time on August 6, killing six members of a family, including two young children.

title: Russian missile strikes on Kyiv kill two
description: Russia attacked Kyiv with waves of ballistic missiles and drones after midnight, killing at least 21 people - three in the capital and 18 in the surrounding region - and injuring more than 45. The assault used 24 ballistic missiles, four Zircon/Onyx missiles and 115 drones, hitting warehouses, a railway station and other civilian infrastructure; air defences intercepted 98 drones.

review.note: Core attack/missile counts supported; sources give 17 combined and later two city deaths, not record 21 with 3+18. Title/number mismatch. Onset after midnight August 5 local implies potentially August 4 UTC; precise onset and final combined toll unresolved.

title: Russian strike on grain ship in Odesa region kills one
description: Russian forces attacked a merchant dry cargo ship flying the flag of Guinea-Bissau and loaded with Ukrainian wheat, damaging the hull and starting a fire. One Ukrainian sailor was killed and three crew members were injured; the crew was evacuated to shore.

review.note: Mera Queen, flag, wheat, one killed/three injured supported. Odesa report dates strike evening August 5; trade publication uses August 6. Preserve conflict rather than treating report date as proof. Exact UTC date requires primary confirmation.

title: Sri Lanka floods and mudslides kill seven
description: Torrential rains triggered floods and mudslides across Sri Lanka's central highlands, killing at least eight people - six in Nuwara Eliya, one in Kandy and one in Puttalam - and affecting more than 16,000 people, with nearly 11,000 evacuated. Authorities closed schools in the affected areas.

review.note: Disaster began before August 5; eight already reported August 4, later nine by August 25. Eight/seven title mismatch. Geographic and time windows differ; exact onset/toll scope and 11000 evacuated unresolved. Do not treat cumulative impacts as August 5 deaths.

title: ATF operation in Nashville ends with man and teenager fatally shot
description: James Salinas, 32, and Denzel Molina, 16, were fatally shot during an ATF firearms operation on Landers Avenue in Nashville on August 6. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said agents encountered two people and gunfire was exchanged; it was investigating the circumstances. No officers were injured.

title: Gaza hospitals report one death from earlier wounds
description: An August 6 medical bulletin reported one Palestinian who died of earlier wounds and five injured people received by Gaza hospitals during the preceding 24 hours. It reported a cumulative death toll of 73,382 since October 2023.

review.note: August 6 is the bulletin date, not a proven death or attack date. The report says one person died of earlier wounds during a rolling 24-hour period; it does not identify Beit Lahia or a new airstrike. Cumulative 73,382 and five wounded are supported. Exact death time and incident linkage remain unresolved.

title: Russian drone strike on Lozova train station kills two
description: Russian drones struck railway infrastructure and the station in Lozova on August 6, killing two railway workers aged 52 and 59 and injuring 11 people, according to regional police.

title: Russian strikes kill six in Balakliia and Sumy region
description: Ukrainian authorities reported three people killed in overnight strikes on homes in Balakliia and three in attacks in Sumy region. Reuters reported at least 19 wounded in Sumy-region settlements, another 12 in Sumy city, and six in a drone attack on a van in Kherson region.

review.note: Reuters supports six deaths, three each in Balakliia and Sumy region, but says overnight without times to determine August 5 versus 6 UTC. Sumy city's guided-bomb attack injured 12, not 13; not all attacks are established as drones. Compare the separate Lozova entry to avoid combining separate attacks.

title: Storm deaths in the Philippines reach at least 27
description: Heavy rains from tropical depressions Luis and Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon killed at least 27 people across the Philippines, with 17 injured and one missing, according to the Office of Civil Defense on August 19. About 5.39 million people were affected across Luzon and Mindanao, with nearly 2,000 homes damaged and 461 evacuation centers housing about 42,000 people. Landslides and flooding were widespread, including 10 killed in Baguio City when a rain-drenched mountainside collapsed on three houses.

review.note: The record is a nationwide cumulative storm series, not a discrete Northern Luzon event on August 6. Official reporting begins July 30; the August 20 OCD figure rose to 29 reported deaths, while later reports add other storms and cannot be substituted without matching scope. Reported versus validated counts also differ. Includes potential overlap with August 9 Baguio and Batangas records; do not add all three totals. Resolve episode boundary and validated toll before replacement.

title: Wildfire kills bulldozer operator in Oregon
description: Jason Ensign, a 47-year-old equipment operator, died while operating a bulldozer at the Wrights Spring Fire in Oregon on August 6. Rapid fire growth cut off his escape route while he helped construct fire lines.

title: Firefighting helicopter crash near Utah wildfire kills two
description: Two pilots died when a contracted CH-54A firefighting helicopter crashed near Kanosh at about 10:41 a.m. local time on August 7 while dropping water on the Widemouth 2 Fire.

title: Thailand school shooting kills nine
description: A student killed his grandparents before attacking Debsirin Nonthaburi School on the morning of August 7, killing five staff members and injuring more than 20 people. The shooter also died. A wounded pupil died on August 8, bringing the reported total, including the shooter and the grandparents, to nine.

title: Explosive drone attack on police substation kills officer in northern Colombia
description: Explosives dropped from drones struck the San Roque police substation in Curumani, Cesar, killing one officer and wounding another. Local reporting places the attack on the night of August 7.

review.note: Local follow-up dates the attack to the night of August 7; without an hour, August 7 versus 8 UTC remains unresolved. One officer killed and another wounded are supported. Remove unrelated tollgate and presidential-term detail rather than treating those as evidence of this incident's date.

title: Helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro kills four
location: Alto da Boa Vista, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
description: A Robinson 44 helicopter crashed in a forested area near Vista Chinesa in the Tijuca National Park in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday morning, killing all four people on board, firefighters said.

title: IS-linked militants kill at least 13 in eastern Congo village attack
location: Banana École, Mambasa, Ituri, DR Congo
description: An attack attributed to ADF militants killed at least 13 civilians in Banana Ecole, Mambasa territory, Ituri. Local reporting described homes and vehicles burned and villagers abducted. Reports disagree whether the attack occurred August 7 or 8.

review.note: Both sources support at least 13 killed and attribution to ADF/IS-linked militants. AP reports Saturday, whereas the local report explicitly says Friday August 7 around 19:00 local (17:00 UTC). This is not merely a publication-date difference that can be silently resolved. Omit the imprecise Uganda-border characterization.

title: Russian drone strike kills three in Brovary district
description: A Russian drone strike destroyed a family home in Brovary district, killing a three-year-old child and his grandparents. Three other family members and a neighbor were hospitalized.

review.note: Three deaths are supported for Brovary, while the wider Kyiv/capital-region total later became four. Do not substitute the wider toll into this narrower record. Later police reporting has four injured, not three. The overnight attack needs a time to distinguish August 7 from 8 UTC.

title: Habagat floods and landslides kill three in Batangas, Philippines
description: Widespread flooding and multiple landslides triggered by the southwest monsoon (habagat) killed three people and left one fisherman missing in Batangas province. One victim, 69-year-old construction worker Teodoro Latumbo, died when a landslide buried his barracks in Barangay Calumala, Santa Teresita, late Saturday night.

review.note: ABS-CBN supports a provincial total of three reported August 9, but its accessible page lacks the narrative needed to date each death. Manila Bulletin places Latumbo's death Saturday night August 8, not August 9. Full three-death chronology remains unresolved. These deaths potentially overlap the nationwide Luis/Maymay/monsoon cumulative record. The provincial/nationwide casualty overlap remains unresolved.

title: Houthi strikes on Mokha kill at least seven in Yemen
description: Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks on the western port city of Mokha on Sunday killed at least seven people - three civilians and four military personnel, according to medical sources - and wounded about 15 others, some critically. The Houthis launched a fresh round of strikes hours later.

review.note: August 9 attack is supported, but later accounts conflict: Reuters quotes the military's seven deaths/30 injured; Anadolu has seven/35; AFP via South24 reports eleven (three civilians, eight military)/32. The record's seven/15 is preliminary and may omit later attack waves. Establish whether the intended scope is the first strike or all Sunday attacks before selecting a replacement toll.

title: Israeli strikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza
description: Israeli strikes across the Gaza Strip killed three Palestinians and wounded nine others on August 9, targeting civilian neighborhoods, displacement camps and areas previously designated as safe, amid ongoing violations of the ceasefire agreement. Gaza's Health Ministry put the cumulative death toll at 73,386.

review.note: The August 9 WAFA bulletin reports two deaths received in 24 hours, including one from earlier wounds, not three new strike deaths on that date. It supports cumulative 73,386. The cited same-day gunfire report describes three injuries, not deaths. Incident-specific support for three killed, nine wounded, and the asserted target locations was not established; do not infer those from cumulative totals.

title: Landslide on rain-soaked hillside in Baguio kills 10
description: A landslide struck houses in Guisad Surong, Baguio, on the evening of August 9 during prolonged monsoon rain. By early August 11, rescuers had accounted for all 13 reported victims: ten died and three survived.

title: Russian missile strike on Kharkiv apartment block kills two
description: Russian missiles struck a high-rise apartment block in Kharkiv's Saltivskyi district on Sunday morning, August 9, killing two people, two men aged 50 and 66, and injuring more than a dozen others, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov.

title: Sofa factory fire in Riyadh kills 16 Bangladeshi workers
description: A fire broke out on Sunday at a sofa manufacturing factory in the Musa Sanaiya industrial area of Riyadh, killing at least 16 Bangladeshi migrant workers, according to Bangladesh's Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry. Ten of the victims were from the Naogaon district and others from Natore and Rajshahi.

title: Two tribal elders shot dead in South Waziristan, Pakistan
location: Toi Khulla, Lower South Waziristan, Pakistan
description: Unidentified gunmen killed tribal elders Haji Gul and Malik Badshah while they traveled toward Zarmilan in Lower South Waziristan on August 9. Police said the attack occurred near Darozanda in Toi Khulla tehsil; both men belonged to the Suleman Khel tribe.

title: Ukrainian drone attack on Belgorod kills six
description: Russian authorities reported six people killed in a drone attack on Belgorod during the night of 8-9 August 2026. The toll increased after another body was recovered from an apartment building. Russia attributed the attack to Ukraine.

review.note: The death toll rose from three to five and then six. Interfax's August 9 evening report attributes the sixth death to recovery of another man's body from the damaged apartment building, citing the regional operational headquarters. This is an update to the same overnight August 8-9 attack, not an additional incident. Exact fatal-strike timing remains insufficient to select August 8 versus 9 UTC; publication remains withheld.

title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake in western Colombia kills at least 331
location: Western Colombia (Choco; Cali, Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo)
description: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia at 12:34 UTC on August 10, with its epicenter near San Jose del Palmar, Choco. UNGRD's September 3 assessment reported 331 deaths and 466,606 people affected. Buildings collapsed and landslides damaged communities in the affected region.

title: Murder-suicide at Chicago elementary school leaves two custodians dead
description: A shooting at Mark Twain Elementary School in Chicago's Garfield Ridge neighborhood on August 10 killed custodian Amalia Bautista Perez, 48, and her 63-year-old coworker. The medical examiner classified their deaths as homicide and suicide respectively. No children were in the school.

title: Palestinian girl dies of wounds from Israeli fire in Gaza
location: Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, Gaza Strip, Palestine
description: Thirteen-year-old Saba Naim Abdullah al-Hashash died on August 10 from wounds sustained when Israeli forces shot her several days earlier in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, according to WAFA.

title: Russian artillery strike on Buhaivka village in Kharkiv region kills five
location: Buhaivka, Chuhuiv district, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine
description: Russian forces carried out a massive artillery strike on the residential area of the village of Buhaivka in the Chuhuiv district of Kharkiv Oblast on August 10, killing five people and destroying several houses, according to regional authorities and the prosecutor's office.

title: Russian strike on Zaporizhstal kills eight workers
description: A Russian ballistic-missile attack struck the Zaporizhstal steel plant around 00:30 local time on August 11, or August 10 UTC. The plant later reported eight employees killed and 26 injured in that attack, which halted production.

title: Russian-installed official reports fatal drone strike on Donetsk fuel station
description: Denis Pushilin, the Russian-installed head of occupied Donetsk, said a Ukrainian drone struck a fuel station in the city's Proletarsky district on August 10, killing a 45-year-old truck driver and wounding an employee.

review.note: The report supports the August 10 claim, 45-year-old truck driver killed and station employee wounded, but derives entirely from the Russian-installed official. No independent confirmation was located. Describe it as his allegation rather than presenting responsibility as independently established. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

title: Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk kills 13
description: A Ukrainian drone attack struck Nizhnekamsk on the morning of August 10. Russian authorities reported 13 deaths and 78 injuries. Ukraine said it targeted an oil refinery in the city.

review.note: Later AP reporting gives 13 killed and 78 injured, superseding 39 injured. Remove the ranking and unsupported child detail from the replacement. Russian officials reported casualties; Ukraine said it targeted a refinery, so do not independently assert intentional civilian targeting. Other retrieved reporting describes the night leading into August 10. No sufficiently precise fatal-strike time was established to distinguish August 9 from 10 UTC; withhold despite the supported toll update.

title: Ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba killing 46
description: An overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba on August 11 after encountering strong waves. Police reported 46 deaths by August 13, while the disaster-management agency said 77 people had been rescued. Authorities had not established a definitive passenger or missing-person count.

title: Ferry fire off Bali kills one
description: The Putri Yasmin ferry caught fire between Bali and Lombok around 4:15 a.m. local time on August 12, or August 11 UTC. Rescuers evacuated 211 people and recovered a 19-year-old Indonesian woman's body, authorities reported.

title: Flash floods in Adré kill three
description: Heavy rains in the afternoon triggered flash floods in several neighborhoods of Adré, a town in the Assoungha department of Ouaddaï Province in eastern Chad, killing three people; local media reported five people were swept away by the water.

review.note: The local August 12 report explicitly dates the rain and flooding to the afternoon of August 11 and supports the town/department/province. Witness accounts describe five swept away, three dead and two rescued; do not treat all five as deaths. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

title: Houthi missile strike on cargo ship Tihama in Bab el-Mandeb kills six
description: Yemen's coastguard reported six people killed, including two rescuers, and ten injured in successive missile strikes on the cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on August 11. Later Indonesian reporting still listed one crewman among the missing, leaving a discrepancy with the initial nationality breakdown.

review.note: August 11 attack and Yemeni coastguard's six reported deaths/ten injuries are corroborated, including two rescuers. However, August 14 Indonesian foreign-ministry reporting still classifies its crewman as missing, whereas earlier reports count him dead. Do not silently resolve that discrepancy or label all six confirmed. A later reconciliation is needed for the confirmed-death total. Ship flag also varies between reports, so omit it.

title: Landslide on Mumbai chawl kills eight
description: A rain-triggered landslide struck homes at Gaushiya Chawl in Chirag Nagar, Mumbai, around 3:48 a.m. local time on August 12, or August 11 UTC. The death toll rose to eight before search operations ended on August 13; seven others were injured.

title: Man kills wife and four children in Winfield, Kansas murder-suicide
description: Police found Ronald H. Williams Sr., 53, Kelly George, 44, and four children aged three to nine dead in a Winfield home on August 11. Williams had called 911 around 8:50 a.m. saying he had killed his family and intended to kill himself. Police investigated the deaths as a murder-suicide.

review.note: Police identify six dead and an 08:50 local 911 call on August 11, also that UTC date. Retrieved reporting establishes the family deaths but not marriage/parentage for every child; omit those ancillary assertions and the imprecise 'early' qualifier. Total includes the suspected perpetrator. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

title: Russian strike on tanker truck in Odesa region kills two
description: A Russian strike hit a tanker truck containing oil residue in Odesa region on August 11. Regional administration head Oleh Kiper reported two people killed and three wounded.

title: Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk region kill five
description: Russian forces carried out massive strikes on the Dnipropetrovsk region on the evening of August 10 and during the night of August 11, killing five people — including three minors — and injuring seven others, according to Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office. Regional authorities earlier reported three dead, including a 15-year-old boy, and five injured, with drone and artillery attacks hitting five districts and damaging logistics facilities.

review.note: Primary police report lists four killed across August 10-11, one aged 15, and eight wounded including three children. Prosecutor reporting places the boy's death on the evening of August 10 and two other minors among injured, not dead. AP initially reported three deaths. The record's five dead/three minors is not established, and the aggregate's UTC period is unresolved.

title: Ukrainian drone attack on Voronezh region kills one
description: Voronezh governor Alexander Gusev reported one person killed and two injured in an overnight drone attack, with falling debris setting warehouse facilities on fire. His statement was reported August 11.

review.note: Reuters supports one death, two injuries and warehouse fires according to the governor. It describes an overnight attack without enough timing to choose August 10 versus 11 UTC. The victim's precise age/district and national 396-drone total were not established from retrieved evidence; use a narrower description once the date is resolved.

title: Beit Lahia drone strike: initial fatality report corrected
description: A drone strike injured two people in Beit Lahia on August 12, 2026. Anadolu corrected an initial report that one person had died: medical sources instead confirmed that the person was critically wounded. This retained archive entry counts no confirmed deaths from the corrected report; the subsequent outcome is not established.

correction.note: Anadolu explicitly corrected the initial fatality report to a critical injury. Preserve the event as a correction, with zero deaths confirmed by the corrected report, rather than deleting it or counting the withdrawn fatality. This does not establish the victim's subsequent outcome.

original_values.title: Israeli fire kills one in Gaza
original_values.description: An Israeli airstrike on Beit Lahia in the northern Gaza Strip killed one Palestinian and wounded five others, the first reported airstrike in about a week, with the Israeli military saying it targeted a Hamas cell commander. Gaza's Health Ministry put the death toll since October 7, 2023 at 73,388 and the number of wounded at 174,259.

title: Landslide in Rolpa district kills ten
description: A landslide triggered by continuous rain swept away nine houses, two cowsheds, a shop and a church in the Kotalbara area of Thabang Rural Municipality in Nepal's western Rolpa district on the night of August 12, 2026, killing 10 people and leaving two missing. Five bodies were recovered at the site and five more were found in neighbouring Pyuthan district, police said.

review.note: August 12 evening at Kotalbara is supported. Initial ten dead/three missing contradicts the record's two missing. Police reported 12 recovered dead and one child missing August 15; August 19 reporting says 13 killed without explaining whether the last missing child was recovered or presumed dead. Confirm that distinction before updating lives_lost. The separate August 13 Sunchhahari landslide is not this event.

title: Military Apache helicopter crash near Salado kills two
description: An AH-64 Apache attack helicopter from Fort Hood crashed into a field south of Salado, Texas, around 1:35 p.m. local time, killing both pilots on board and igniting a grass fire that forced nearby residents to flee.

title: Russian drone strikes on Kherson kill two
description: Russian strike drones killed two people in Kherson overnight on August 12, including a woman struck inside her home, and wounded others in the Tsentralnyi district, according to regional authorities and military administration head Oleksandr Prokudin.

review.note: The overnight attack killed two, including a woman inside her home, and injured two in Tsentralnyi district. Available reporting does not give the strike time needed to choose August 11 or 12 UTC. A separately reported August 12 afternoon fatal strike must not be silently merged.

title: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia region kill one
description: Russia carried out more than 1,000 strikes on Zaporizhzhia and the surrounding region over the day, killing one person and wounding at least eight, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said. An overnight drone attack destroyed the Epicentr shopping center in the city, sparking a large fire and power outages, and damaged residential buildings.

review.note: The 1,000-plus strikes and one death refer to August 11, reported August 12, with nine wounded. The Epicentr attack is a separate overnight event. The record conflates a daily casualty aggregate with the shopping-center strike; the fatal incident time/identity must be resolved before assigning a single UTC date.

title: Severe storms and tornadoes kill three in US Midwest
description: Three deaths were reported amid the August 11 Midwest storms: a child struck by a falling tree in Indiana, a person killed in a Portage house explosion whose cause was under investigation, and an Ohio resident whom emergency responders could not reach because of flooding.

review.note: Reports published August 12 describe Tuesday August 11 storms. Three associated deaths are reported, but the Portage house-explosion cause was still being investigated and the Ohio death was an indirect emergency-access death. Exact UTC times of the geographically separate deaths were not established. Do not present all three as direct tornado deaths or use publication date as occurrence date.

title: Ukrainian attacks on Belgorod region kill two civilians
description: Ukrainian forces attacked Russia's Belgorod region more than 170 times over 24 hours, killing two civilians in the Belgorodsky and Graivoronsky districts and injuring three others, acting Governor Alexander Shuvayev said. RIA Novosti later reported three dead and seven people seeking medical help.

review.note: TASS establishes a past-24-hour bulletin on August 12 with two killed and three wounded, not two deaths necessarily occurring August 12 UTC. The record itself juxtaposes a later three-death report without establishing whether it updates the same incidents. Resolve individual victims and reporting interval before choosing a toll/date.

title: Ukrainian attacks on Krasnodar region kill three
description: Governor Veniamin Kondratyev reported three deaths, including an eight-year-old child, and 24 injuries in overnight attacks across Krasnodar region. Novorossiysk's port infrastructure and grain terminals were also damaged.

review.note: Three deaths/24 injuries apply to Krasnodar region, not solely Novorossiysk; the child is specifically linked to the city. Overnight timing leaves August 11/12 UTC unresolved. The supported scope correction below avoids attributing all regional casualties to the port.

title: Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea kills civilian
description: A civilian was killed in the village of Novosyolovskoye in the Razdolnensky district of Crimea in an overnight Ukrainian drone attack, regional head Sergey Aksyonov said.

review.note: Both reports relay Aksyonov's claim of one civilian death in Novosyolovskoye during the night leading into August 12. Without an incident time, the UTC date could be August 11 or 12. Attribution is a Russian-installed official's claim, not independent verification.

title: Armed man fatally shot by police at Auckland shopping centre
description: An armed man fleeing from police was shot and killed at Sylvia Park Shopping Centre in Auckland on Thursday afternoon. Police said the man had stolen an air rifle from a gun shop in Penrose; he was confronted under an overpass and pronounced dead at the scene despite first aid.

title: Bomb blast kills defected naval officer in Sevastopol
description: An explosion in Sevastopol on the morning of August 13 killed a Russian naval officer later identified in reporting as Robert Shageyev, a former Ukrainian submarine commander who defected in 2014. Russian authorities said they detained a woman and alleged Ukrainian intelligence involvement; that allegation was not independently verified.

title: Car crash into truck in Nagpur kills two students
description: Two 17-year-old students died and a third teenager was seriously injured when their car hit a stationary truck in Nagpur early on August 12 local time. Police said they had gone for a drive while waiting for a friend's birthday celebration.

review.note: NDTV's August 13 article explicitly says early Wednesday morning, August 12, and local August 12 reporting corroborates that day. UTC could be August 11 or 12 without the crash time. Two dead and one injured are supported. The teenagers were taking a drive while awaiting a birthday celebration, not necessarily traveling to the party.

title: Explosion at Fujian shipyard kills firefighter
description: A fire at Huahai Shipyard in Gantang, Fu'an, began at 13:09 local time on August 13. An explosion at 14:10 injured ten firefighters and two other people; one firefighter died in hospital that evening. Authorities were investigating the cause.

title: Explosion at Port of Rotterdam kills one
description: An explosion at the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands killed at least one person and injured several others on August 13, 2026. Dutch regional broadcaster Rijnmond reported the blast occurred at around 11:30 a.m. local time; Rotterdam police said the cause remained under investigation and emergency services scaled up their response.

title: Explosion during ordnance disposal in Sevastopol kills five
description: Five people were killed on August 13, 2026, during the clearance and disposal of explosive ordnance following a Ukrainian UAV attack on Sevastopol, Russian media reported. Four of the dead were pyrotechnicians of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations (EMERCOM) and one was a security guard.

review.note: EMERCOM confirms four personnel deaths and Reuters adds the security guard, quoting the governor's disposal-after-drone-attack account. EMERCOM says the night of August 13 without an exact time, so August 12 versus 13 UTC remains unresolved. Crimea should be identified as occupied Ukrainian territory.

title: Fire at Greater Noida wood-cutting shop kills one worker
location: Shahberi, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India
description: A fire at a wood-cutting shop in Shahberi, Greater Noida West, left Altamas dead and Aman injured. Police said both were rescued unconscious and taken to hospital after the overnight fire on August 13-14.

review.note: PTI dates the fire to the intervening night of August 13-14, not a precise time. One died; the other was later stable, not necessarily still critical. An exact time is needed for UTC. Full ThePrint open was denied; indexed PTI text supports the incident and rescue.

title: Firecracker factory explosion near Sivakasi kills two workers
description: Two men died after an explosion while testing a new chemical-mixing machine at a fireworks factory near Sivakasi on August 13. One died at the site and the second in hospital. Police opened an investigation into the cause.

title: Israeli strikes kill two Palestinians in Gaza
description: Israeli strikes killed Gaza police official Jamal Abu Kamil in Gaza City and Hudhaifa Kawara in Khan Younis on August 13, according to Palestinian medical and interior-ministry sources. Israel said Abu Kamil was a Hamas commander.

title: Landslide and water seepage in Chamoli tunnel kills seven workers
description: A sudden influx of water and debris entered the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti project's unfinished tunnel in Chamoli around 6:20 p.m. local time on August 13. At least seven workers died and others were injured, with searches continuing for missing workers.

title: Mudslide in Changxing, Zhejiang kills one and leaves three missing
description: A rain-triggered mudslide collapsed a house in Tanlongqiao village, Heping town, Changxing, around 6:30 a.m. local time on August 14, or August 13 UTC. County authorities reported one confirmed death and three people missing that afternoon.

title: Multi-vehicle crash near Accra kills at least 11
description: A multi-vehicle collision on the Accra-Kumasi highway at Ofankor Barrier in Ghana's capital killed at least 11 people and injured 13 others in the early hours of August 13, 2026, according to the Ghana National Fire Service. The service said it received a distress call at about 4:00 a.m. local time regarding the collision.

title: Record rainfall in Chiba kills thirteen
description: Record rainfall on August 13-14 flooded communities in Chiba Prefecture. The governor reported thirteen deaths, one person missing and damage to more than 4,500 homes by August 27.

title: Russian drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia kills five
description: Russian forces launched a combined drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia in the early hours, damaging buildings and industrial facilities and causing fires and power outages. Five people were killed and at least 20 were injured, according to the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, Ivan Fedorov.

review.note: The matching five-dead/20-injured report is dated August 11, with its update at 02:10 local, and describes the August 10-11 attack. This strongly duplicates the original August 11 'Russian combined strike on Zaporizhzhia kills seven' row, whose toll later reached eight and UTC date is August 10. No separate August 13 five-death event was established. Withhold this duplicate candidate pending identity reconciliation; do not publish both.

title: Russian drone strike on passenger train in Odesa region kills two
description: A Russian drone struck a passenger train in Berezivka district, Odesa region, on August 13, killing the driver and his assistant. Authorities evacuated the 340 passengers, including 67 children; no passengers were reported injured.

title: Suspected murder-suicide shooting on Staten Island kills two
location: Staten Island, New York, United States
description: Police responded to a shooting at a Garth Court home on Staten Island around 11:10 a.m. on August 13. Dana Foley, 39, died at the scene, while Dakota Suckstorff, 27, died after being taken to hospital. Police investigated a suspected murder-suicide.

title: Coal mine explosion in Cucunuba kills six miners
description: Six miners died in a methane-associated explosion at the Porvenir 1 coal mine in Cucunuba on August 14. Colombia's National Mining Agency confirmed the deaths and ordered operations suspended pending compliance with safety requirements.

title: Helicopter crash in Sehmatal, Saxony kills pilot
description: A helicopter crashed and caught fire during forestry work near Neudorf in Sehmatal on the morning of August 14. Workers pulled the 29-year-old pilot from the aircraft, but he died at the scene. Police received the report at 9:55 a.m. and opened an investigation with the aviation accident authority.

title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Flores kills at least 68
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Flores at 21:58 UTC on August 14, or 5:58 a.m. local time on August 15. BNPB reported 68 identified deaths by August 17. The earthquake damaged buildings, triggered landslides and small tsunami waves, and displaced residents.

title: RSF attack on Um Arada reportedly kills at least eighteen
description: An RSF attack on Um Arada southwest of El Obeid on August 14 killed at least eighteen people and wounded seventeen, according to local-source reporting carried by Europa Press. Rights and local reports documented more than fourteen civilian deaths and displacement toward El Obeid.

title: Russian double drone strike on Sumy region kills woman and nine-year-old boy
description: Russian forces launched a double strike with jet-powered UAVs on a private home in the Buryn community of Ukraine's Sumy region early on August 14, 2026, killing a 29-year-old woman and her nine-year-old son and wounding four others, including the boy's father and grandmother who were hospitalized with severe burns. The attack caused extensive damage and sparked a fire, according to the Sumy Regional Military Administration.

title: Russian glide bomb hits apartment block in Donetsk region, killing one
description: A Russian guided-bomb attack damaged an apartment building in Kramatorsk, killing one person and injuring others. Reports published August 14 described an overnight strike, with the reported injury count later rising to 22.

review.note: The attack is in Kramatorsk and one death is supported. Injury reports increased from 16/17 to 22. Overnight timing leaves August 13 versus 14 UTC unresolved. Omit the precise floors-destroyed count rather than retain an unchecked structural detail.

title: Series of shootings in Michigan kills six including gunman
description: Five people were killed in shootings in Missaukee County on August 14, and suspect Chad Hickman, 39, was later found dead. Police found victims at two homes and in woods near Whitlock Lake; another person was critically injured. The six-death total includes the suspect.

title: Toxic gas at Sitakunda shipbreaking yard kills ten workers
description: Workers at Ferdous Steel's Sitakunda shipbreaking yard were exposed to toxic gas inside a vessel on August 14. Authorities identified hydrogen sulfide. The reported death toll rose to ten after another worker died in hospital on August 19.

title: Flash flood and landslide in Ponferrada area kill two women
description: A flash flood and debris flow struck Manzanedo de Valdueza and nearby settlements in the Ponferrada area on August 15, killing two women. Four other people, including two children, were injured. An elderly man initially missing was found unharmed.

title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 including women and children
description: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported eleven deaths in Israeli strikes on Ansar and Deir Zahrani during the night leading into August 15 local time: seven in Ansar, including three children, and four in Deir Zahrani. Nineteen people were reported wounded.

review.note: The ministry's eleven deaths (seven Ansar, four Deir Zahrani) and nineteen wounded are supported. Accounts describe overnight/dawn strikes without enough precise timing for both sites to assign one UTC date. Strip ancillary flight, building-height and condemnation details, but retain the date blocker.

title: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian in Khan Younis
description: Fourteen-year-old Suhail Masoud Shalouf was shot by Israeli forces on al-Tina Street south of Khan Younis on the evening of August 15, according to WAFA. The Palestinian Red Crescent recovered his body the following day.

title: Polish tourist bus overturns on Hungarian motorway killing 12
description: A bus carrying 57 Polish passengers and two drivers overturned on Hungary's M3 motorway near Mezokeresztes at about 01:00 local time on August 16, killing 12 people. Emergency services later reported 47 injured, including 10 seriously. Police detained the driver.

title: Russian drone strike on Marhanets kills three-month-old baby
description: Russian forces struck a multi-storey building in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region, with drones during a nighttime attack, killing a three-month-old boy and injuring 11 people, including children, according to regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue and clearance operations continued at the site.

review.note: The three-month-old boy's death and eleven injured, including two children, are supported. The official account says nighttime; no strike time was located to distinguish August 14 and 15 UTC.

title: Shooting at Lexington, Kentucky park kills one and injures four
